{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZcKLmQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDDZbo", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 47, "title": "Resolve and implement CGRAM data-port addressing during display", "body": "## Problem

CGRAM data ports always access the software-selected address, regardless of display state. In baseline `bd0eecab0adf064c3db4f70289bedd781eed1996`, [`Ppu::write`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/bd0eecab0adf064c3db4f70289bedd781eed1996/crates/snes-core/src/ppu.rs#L226) uses `caddr` directly for `$2122`; [`Ppu::read`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/bd0eecab0adf064c3db4f70289bedd781eed1996/crates/snes-core/src/ppu.rs#L287) does the same for `$213B`. Neither path considers forced blank, raster position, or rendering ownership.

The [existing CGRAM regressions](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/bd0eecab0adf064c3db4f70289bedd781eed1996/crates/snes-core/tests/regression.rs#L607) establish selected blanked write-pair behavior. They do not establish display-access rules or mixed read/write phase behavior. The README explicitly retains CGRAM access/corruption as unresolved. This is the next prerequisite identified in the supplied latest assessment; no open Issue duplicates it.

## Expected outcome

Implement the smallest source-supported correction to CGRAM display-time addressing through `$2121/$2122/$213B`, preserving documented byte sequencing and existing legal palette transfers.

**Resolve the CGRAM-specific specification before changing production behavior.** The repository records reference versions, but its ignored raw specification copies are absent from this checkout. This planning inspection therefore does not establish an exact CGRAM access window or corruption address. Do not turn either into an invented hardware requirement.

Use these specification authorities:

- [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm): CGRAM palette-memory access and register descriptions, INIDISP, and PPU memory-access timing.
- [Anomie's Register Doc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt): register flag legend, `$2121` CGADD, `$2122` CGDATA, `$213B` CGDATAREAD, and relevant display/memory-access qualifications.
- The repository's [reference record](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/bd0eecab0adf064c3db4f70289bedd781eed1996/docs/issue-45-validation.md#specification-reconciliation-recorded-before-production-changes) identifies Fullsnes no$sns v1.5 and Anomie revision 1157. Record the actual versions, hashes, sections, and disagreements used for this correction.

Before implementation, derive an explicit operation/state table covering:

| Operation | Semantics to establish and preserve or correct |
| --- | --- |
| `$2121` write | Color-address assignment; reset of read/write byte selection; whether the pending data latch changes. |
| First `$2122` byte | Low-byte latch capture, memory-commit behavior, and address/phase progression. |
| Second `$2122` byte | Paired commit, seven-bit high-byte storage, destination selection, and wrap. |
| `$213B` read | Low/high selection, address advancement, interaction with pending writes, and high-byte bit 7 from the PPU2 read bus. |
| Display ownership | Software-addressed versus rendering-owned access during forced blank, ordinary VBlank, visible display, HBlank, and scanline 0. |

The existing accessible-period contract stages a low write without committing memory, commits both bytes on the following high write, masks the stored high byte to seven bits, and wraps across color `$FF`. Existing readback returns the high byte with PPU2's retained bit 7. Preserve these supported cases unless the specification reconciliation demonstrates a correction. A shared cursor in the implementation alone proves neither shared nor independent hardware read/write phases.

Replace unconditional software-addressed access where the reconciled sources establish a different access or ownership rule. Do not copy VRAM's HBlank prohibition, OAM's substitute address, blanket write suppression, or a fixed read value into CGRAM without support. Separate documented behavior from any necessary deterministic approximation. Exact electrical corruption values may remain unresolved without blocking a supported correction.

Scope is this CGRAM port behavior and its CPU/DMA/HDMA integration. Non-goals include a pixel-fetch pipeline, complete raster effects, PAL, overscan/interlace, unrelated rendering or DMA timing changes, and commercial compatibility claims.

## Context and reproduction

A minimal original reproduction should initialize distinct palette sentinels during forced blank, select a different software address, and access `$2122/$213B` during stable visible display. Compare the resulting access/ownership effects with forced-blank, VBlank, and HBlank controls using the reconciled contract. Include literal before/after results that distinguish the correction from this baseline; do not assert an unknown corruption byte as a hardware oracle.

CPU accesses and DMA/HDMA already share PPU register decoding. [`SystemBus::transfer`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/bd0eecab0adf064c3db4f70289bedd781eed1996/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L461) samples reverse transfers after four clocks and commits destinations after eight. These are retained model conventions, not independently verified physical strobes.

The [source-built HDMA fixture](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/bd0eecab0adf064c3db4f70289bedd781eed1996/tools/ppu-test.py) checks eleven palette-derived grayscale bands. Preserve it; its success does not establish every CGRAM access boundary.

Planning was read-only. No tests were rerun and no files were changed.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record the specification reconciliation and exact operation/state table before production changes. Distinguish explicit statements, derivations, conflicts, and unresolved behavior. Correct unsupported earlier contracts or tests with evidence rather than preserving them solely because they passed.
- [ ] Implement the supported CGRAM addressing/access correction in the shared PPU port path. Show at least one concrete baseline counterexample fixed by the production change. Document any approximation separately from hardware semantics.
- [ ] Add original, independent numerical vectors covering both byte phases, mixed reads/writes, readdressing with a pending low byte, `$FF` wrap, high-byte masking, and independently seeded CPU/PPU1/PPU2 bus values. Expected results must not call production helpers.
- [ ] Add natural-scheduler CPU tests for forced blank, VBlank, stable visible display, HBlank, scanline 0, and recovery after restricted access. Exercise relevant boundaries before/at/after using documented coordinates or explicitly labeled scheduler conventions. Do not claim physical boundary accuracy from model tests.
- [ ] Cover repeated-port forward and reverse DMA plus direct/indirect HDMA controls in both directions. Assert applicable phase/latch effects, payloads, address/count progression, and termination. Preserve legal HBlank palette transfers and existing DMA/HDMA ordering regressions.
- [ ] Add an original in-memory LoROM guest in `crates/snes-core/tests/ppu_cgram_access.rs`. CPU instructions must initialize, synchronize, perform accesses, and publish numeric WRAM results and a completion marker. Bound execution to 150,000 instructions and fewer than four frame wraps; the host must not inject raster state, port phases, or expected results. Document original MIT source/data provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`.
- [ ] Run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, and `cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test ppu_cgram_access`. Preserve existing CGRAM, VRAM, OAM/reload, counter-latch, color, DMA/HDMA, CPU, SPC, and DSP regressions.
- [ ] Run the [README validation gates](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/bd0eecab0adf064c3db4f70289bedd781eed1996/README.md#validate): diagnostic regeneration/comparison; pinned assembler builds including SPC; source-built CPU/SPC suites; `tools/ppu-test.py`; two fresh cleared-game builds; production web build; and `npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'` after dependency/Chromium setup. Preserve Castle's five-minute replay and full route, Memory's gameplay/music/effect assertions, Pages smoke checks, source pins, hashes, and replay inputs. Use only original or provenance-cleared source-built artifacts.
- [ ] Record actual commands/results and baseline failures. Update README limitations honestly. `ppu-ports` remains partial: exact rendering-owned corruption, unresolved phase/latch retention, physical access/blanking latency, and dot-level arbitration remain outstanding wherever unsupported or untested. Preserve the scope and status of all 24 inventory categories; limited passes establish neither full accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

Additional independent, explicitly licensed source-built CGRAM diagnostics. No commercial ROM or firmware acquisition is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
